candidates.title: Specify TLV framing and tag admission bounds
candidates.observed: Tlv.Create parses the first item without checking that the remaining span is empty, although its input says and nothing more. Constructor tags are any 0..FFFF integer, emitted by minimal integer width, whereas the parser recognizes a two-byte tag only when the first octet's low five bits are 1F and never follows additional continuation bytes. candidates.title: Check ARKG native allocation and conversion outcomes at their actual calls
candidates.observed: Native wrappers construct SafeHandles without throwing on zero handles, use DangerousGetHandle to call native functions, and callers discard BN_bn2binpad results when exporting coordinates/shared secrets. OpenSSL 3.0.0 original BN conversion documentation returns NULL on BN_bin2bn error and a byte count or -1 for BN_bn2binpad. The managed wrappers alone do not establish native release, constant-time scalar handling, allocation-failure behavior or available exports on each target platform.
candidates.desired: Record checked-allocation/conversion and secret-native-point cleanup as Pass-2 review inputs. B4 owns the loader/package availability qualification; keep C's conclusions limited to actual ARKG call sites and retain native-shim internals as an external source gap.
candidates.confidence: high managed source; original OpenSSL API contract read; packaged shim/runtime behavior unexecuted
candidates.final_observation: OpenSSL 3.0.0 point/free and EVP_MAC originals inspected: point clear_free explicitly erases sensitive contents, while SDK SafeEcPoint calls the ordinary free export even for shared-secret points. Allocation NULL and BN written-count handling remain actual-call follow-ups. ComputeEcdhSharedSecret's scalar span has no explicit 32-byte admission, while production Derive supplies 32 bytes. The exact NativeShims binary/export/provider implementation remains B4-owned external qualification; C supplies no new Windows/macOS/Linux acceptance claim.

candidates.title: Make SCP parameter containment ownership visible to B6 and applet editors
candidates.observed: The narrowly read parameter boundary differs by layer: SessionCreationOptions borrows SCP parameters and presence service; Scp03KeyParameters stores the supplied StaticKeys reference and disposes that same object; StaticKeys clones source spans. Scp11KeyParameters copies the certificate collection but retains each certificate and the EC private-key reference, then disposes those same objects. Its public key is retained without disposal. Record with-expressions can share the contained disposable owners. XML calls OceKeyRef required for a/c although the constructor does not require it, and claims empty/null b fields while the full constructor accepts supplied values for b.
candidates.desired: B6 should describe construction/containment/disposal and alias lifetime explicitly, and reconcile required-versus-optional metadata with its actual SCP initializer. Cross-reference the same ownership in Security Domain/OpenPGP/PIV examples. Keep record cloning and disposed-alias policy as consequential decisions rather than changing APIs in Pass 1.
candidates.primary_owner: B6-wire-scp; applet-specific caller dispositions stay with boundary owners
candidates.confidence: high for narrowly inspected containment boundary; no wire, certificate-profile or full B6 audit
candidates.final_observation: Narrow Scp11X963Kdf dependency read supports current C provider-test assertions: exported D arrays, shared-secret arrays, concatenation owner and receipt buffers have separate finally scopes; receipt comparison failure and provider Dispose failure are modeled in existing tests. No full SCP wire review or GlobalPlatform-source download was undertaken. Parameter-clone/certificate containment facts and initializer OCE-reference/profile questions remain B6 referrals, with source hashes and unchanged-path disposition retained. HsmAuth CLI shared callers omit deviceContext.SessionOptions; boundary owners should compare that with intended SCP/presence option propagation rather than C claiming universal callback adoption.
